15. X was the first person to liquefy hydrogen (at -252°C) in 1898. He was obsessed with being the first to reach "Absolute Zero." He was convinced he would also be the first to liquefy helium. However, he was beaten to the punch by the Dutch physicist Heike Kamerlingh Onnes in 1908. X was so devastated by this "defeat" that he reportedly became even more reclusive, focusing his later years on the study of soap bubbles. In his final years, the man who conquered liquid hydrogen spent his time blowing giant soap bubbles in the basement of the Royal Institution studying surface tension and thin films. He managed to keep a single soap bubble alive for over a year (376 days) by keeping it in a dust-free, controlled environment. Id X.
